misconception.description: setting the price by adding the target margin percentage to the cost, which applies the percentage to the cost instead of to the selling price

worked_example.text: A shop buys a lamp for EUR 30 and wants a gross margin of 25% of the selling price.
worked_example.solution: If the margin is a quarter of the price, the cost is the other three quarters: price = 30 / 0.75 = EUR 40. Check: the margin is 40 - 30 = EUR 10, which is a quarter of 40. Adding 25% to the cost would have given EUR 37.50, a margin of only 20%.

problem.text: A retailer buys an item for EUR 51 and wants a gross margin of 40% of the selling price. What price should it set?

distractors.note: the documented misconception: adding the margin percentage to the cost, which is a markup on cost
dividing by the margin instead of by one minus the margin

hints: A gross margin is always measured against the selling price, while a markup is measured against the cost. The question names a margin, so decide what share of the price the cost has to be.
If the margin takes 40% of the price, the cost is the remaining 60% of it. Write that as an equation: cost equals price times 0.6.
Rearrange the equation: divide the cost by one minus the target margin to recover the price.
worked_solution: Step 1: read the percentage correctly. The margin is measured on the selling price, so the cost is what is left: 1 - 0.4 = 0.6 of the price. Step 2: write the relationship: 51 = price x 0.6. Step 3: divide: 51 / 0.6 = EUR 85.00. Check it: the gross profit is 85 - 51 = EUR 34, and 34 / 85 is 40% of the price, as required. Adding 40% to the cost instead would give EUR 71.40, where the gross profit of EUR 20.40 is only 28.6% of the price, because the percentage was applied to the smaller base.

far_transfer.text: A wholesaler sells a case of goods for EUR 108 and earns a gross margin of 25% of that selling price. What does the case cost the wholesaler?

distractors.note: reporting the gross profit rather than the cost
treating the 25% as a markup on cost rather than a margin on price
